labels: predictions by the builder (Opus) from the band's algebra and the interior spike's table; the first step's predictions (resolution, floor) were sent before any run and are copied here unchanged; everything under seen_before was measured before this file
seen_before: the interior spike's leak table (straight periodic tube, a full occlusion one diameter long, wall material): 7.3e-3 / 1.26e-3 / 2.4e-4 at D/h 16 / 32 / 64 with the 0.1h interior, 9.0e-5 / 1.45e-5 / 2.7e-6 with 0.01h

an exploratory run of the share form only (laptop, float64, this file's parent tree, a long plug filling the period, steady Stokes, D = 1, nu = rho = 1, g = 8, box 2 cells along z): Q / Q_Brinkman - 1 = +1.10 / +2.24 / +3.06 / +2.19 / +1.81 % at D/h 16 and +0.45 / +1.00 / +1.36 / +0.80 / +0.41 % at D/h 32, for sqrt(K)/h = 0.03 / 0.1 / 0.3 / 1 / 3; the projected CG took 5 to 44 iterations. Against Darcy's G K pi R^2 / mu (the unresolved Brinkman layer's deficit 2 sqrt(K)/R removed) the two sqrt(K)/h = 0.03 points read +0.34 % and +0.07 % [arithmetic]: the first step's 'under 0.1 %' against Brinkman is refuted at D/h 16 and 32 by that seen number, and is kept below unchanged as the prediction it was

operating_point.platform: CPU; GitHub runners (4 vCPU) for the measurements and rates, this laptop for single gate runs
operating_point.sizes_and_parameters: a straight periodic tube along z, D = 1 (R = 0.5), nu = rho = 1, a body force g = 8 on the fluid; steady Stokes (the steady limit of IMEX Euler) unless stated; the default band (W 2h, delta 0.3h); the stiff interior 0.1h or 0.01h as stated; D/h 16 and 32 (64 on the probes); a plug a solid circular cylinder coaxial with the tube unless stated
operating_point.seeds_and_draws: Hypothesis draws at physical scales (sqrt(K)/h 0.01 to 10, a plug's radius 0.2 R to 1.2 R, its length 0.5 D to the period, its centre within the lumen); the controls' rates 200 draws on Actions unless stated

measure_1_resolution.claim: how the bulk Darcy flux of a plug filling the tube comes out when its Brinkman layer is not resolved, the plain sum against the share rule, and from what sqrt(K)/h the profile is right
measure_1_resolution.case: a long plug (longer than the period, so no ends) of the lumen's radius; the box 2 cells along z; the node's lumen flux against Brinkman's Q_B = (G K pi R^2 / mu)(1 - 2 sqrt(K) I1(R/sqrt K) / (R I0(R/sqrt K))), G = rho g

prediction.value: plain: Q/Q_B - 1 = (1 + h/R)^2 - 1 = +26.6 / +12.9 / +6.3 % at D/h 16 / 32 / 64 for sqrt(K)/h <= 0.1; share: |Q/Q_B - 1| < 0.1 %; the profile within about 2 % of the centreline from sqrt(K)/h about 1
prediction.basis: derived (the first step's, unchanged): in the wall's band the plug's own ramp is 1 - chi, so the plain sum's resistivity (1 - chi)/K cancels the drive's (1 - chi) and the Darcy velocity G K / mu reaches R + h; the share rule's 1/K across the fluid of the band leaves the integral of (1 - chi), within 0.19 (h/R)^2 of pi R^2
prediction.why: the operating point is the done case's regime, sqrt(K) far under h

measure_1_resolution.metric: the lumen's flux (the whole box's axial flux over the period), the quantity a pressure drop is read from

measure_2_floor.claim: the floor: the flux an impermeable plug filling the tube lets through the wall's solid around it, over the open tube's
measure_2_floor.case: a plug of the lumen's radius, one diameter long, sqrt(K)/h = 1e-3 (its Darcy flux about 1e-6 of the open tube's), in a period of four diameters; the same box with no plug

prediction.value: within 3 times of the interior spike's 7.3e-3 / 1.26e-3 / 2.4e-4 (0.1h) and 9.0e-5 / 1.45e-5 / 2.7e-6 (0.01h)
prediction.basis: measured-before (the interior spike's occlusion, of wall material); the plug's resistivity blocks the lumen and the band's fluid as the occlusion's did, and adds nothing to the solid beyond
prediction.why: the bypass runs through the band's solid half and the interior's ramp, the same in both

measure_2_floor.metric: Q_leak / Q_open, compared at the build with the plug's own Darcy flux over the open tube's, 8 K L_box / (R^2 L)

measure_3_face.claim: the plug's face against free fluid: the shift, in cells, of the plug's radius that makes the exact Brinkman-core and Stokes-annulus flux equal the measured one
measure_3_face.case: a long coaxial plug of radius 0.5 R in the tube (a gap of 0.25 D), its flux against the composite closed form

prediction.value: +0.7 to +1.0 cells (outward: the plug reads larger) at sqrt(K)/h 0.03; +0.4 to +0.8 at 0.1; within +-0.2 at 0.3 and above
prediction.basis: derived, rough: a stiff band holds the flow where its ramp first reaches about K/h^2, near the band's fluid edge; at sqrt(K)/h near 0.3 the plug's ramp is the calibrated band's own depth
prediction.why: B3: a stiff penalty in a smooth band moves its effective wall

measure_3_face.metric: the fitted radius's shift in cells, which predicts the annulus's flux error (its flux goes as the gap cubed)

measure_4_cost.claim: the projected CG's iterations with a plug, against the same box without one

prediction.value: within 2 times of the box without a plug at the same interior, at every sqrt(K)/h measured
prediction.basis: guess, after the exploratory 5 to 44 iterations on a 2-cell box (seen_before)
prediction.why: Jacobi scales the plug's large diagonal away; the stiff interior already sets the count

gate_1_darcy.claim: a finite plug filling the tube gives Darcy's pressure drop, dp = mu L Q / (K pi R^2) (with Brinkman's wall factor), and the tube's flux the series closed form, within the measured resolution error, over K and resolution
gate_1_darcy.case: a plug of the lumen's radius, one diameter long, in a period of four diameters; Q against rho g L_box / (8 mu (L_box - L) / (pi R^4) + mu L / (K pi R^2 F_B)), F_B Brinkman's factor; the plug's dp read as rho g L_box less the open part's Poiseuille drop at the measured Q
gate_1_darcy.operating_point: sqrt(K)/h 0.1, 0.3, 1; D/h 16, 32; the 0.01h interior (the leak's share under 1e-3) and the 0.1h one (the leak's share added to the line)

prediction.value: within 2 % of the series form at D/h 32 and 4 % at D/h 16 with the 0.01h interior; with 0.1h, high by the leak's share F / (8 K L_box / (R^2 L)) on top
prediction.basis: measured-before (the exploratory long-plug numbers, seen_before) and derived (the leak's share)
prediction.why: the plug's resistance is nearly all of the series

gate_1_darcy.metric: the lumen's flux; the plug's dp follows from it

control.plant: the plug's permeability read 2 % high in the step
control.expected_rate: N/N where the gate's line is under 2 % (D/h 32, 0.01h); the gate states the range it cannot discriminate

gate_1_darcy.cannot_discriminate_if: the leak's share is not under the line (0.1h at small K): the gate then reads the floor, not Darcy

gate_2_brinkman_profile.claim: where sqrt(K) is resolved the profile in a long plug is Brinkman's, u = (G K / mu)(1 - I0(r / sqrt K) / I0(R / sqrt K))
gate_2_brinkman_profile.case: a long plug of the lumen's radius; the axial velocity at the cells' centres within R - 2h against the closed form

prediction.value: the largest error at most 2 % of u_B(0) at D/h 32, about halving from D/h 16
prediction.basis: guess, from the wall's calibrated first-order shift
prediction.why: first order at the wall, second in the fluid

gate_3_annulus.claim: a plug with an annular gap splits the flux as the exact Brinkman core matched to a Stokes annulus (parallel resistances as sqrt(K)/gap goes to zero); the wall's leak judged against B3's line
gate_3_annulus.case: a long coaxial plug of radius 0.5 R; total and plug fluxes against the composite closed form

prediction.value: the total within 3 % and the plug's share within 5 % at D/h 32; below sqrt(K)/h 0.3 the face's shift (measure 3) sets the error, stated as the range's edge
prediction.why: the gap carries nearly all the flux; its error is the plug face's shift

control.plant: the plug's radius read a quarter cell larger

gate_4_resistivities_add.claim: a plug overlapping the wall's band reads the sum of the two resistivities at every face, and nothing else
gate_4_resistivities_add.case: the node's fields with a drawn plug against the wall's fields alone and the plug's alone

prediction.unit: the largest difference, in the field's own rounding

control.plant: the larger of the two in place of their sum

gate_5_positivity.claim: a permeability of zero or below (or not finite) is refused on every draw: at the build where it is declared, and after the run where a study or a range moved it there

prediction.why: the value kind is above zero; the step checks the sampled field and the leaf

gate_6_ledger.claim: with the ledger attached the step identity closes with the plug's Darcy loss booked under its law, at rounding, and the loss equals the drive's work through the plug in a steady flow

prediction.value: the identity's residual within its rounding floor on every draw; the plug's loss within 1e-6 of Q dp_plug dt at a converged steady state
prediction.why: the porous term is one more hosted dissipation, paired at the step's solution

control.plant: the plug's loss booked with its sign flipped

gate_7_gradients.claim: derivatives of the box's flux in the plug's permeability, its centre (off the axis) and its length, forward and reverse, equal central differences in float64

prediction.value: within 1e-6 relative (K) and 1e-4 (geometry, the band's ripple being the discretisation's own)
prediction.why: the field is a smooth function of its leaves away from the switches

control.plant: stop_gradient on the plug's field values

gate_8_float32.claim: float32 gives gate 1's and gate 3's fluxes within its rounding floor of float64's where it resolves them; the range where it does not is stated

prediction.value: within 1e-4 relative at sqrt(K)/h >= 0.1, D/h 16 and 32
prediction.why: the solve's float32 tolerance 1e-5 and its floor

bits.cases: every released program and every merged program with no plug, base origin/release/v0.3.0 against the head, one job, one CPU, one thread (bit_compare.py)
